themes.title: Frontier labs endorse an AI slowdown as markets wobble
themes.summary: For the first time, the four largest AI labs jointly endorsed a slower development pace, prioritising safety over growth. The coordinated stance rattled Asian chip stocks and equity futures, while top executives publicly warned of existential risks. It is a turning point in how frontier labs frame the race they have been driving.
themes.angle: The frontier race now has a self-imposed brake; compute sellers and AI-linked equities repriced within hours.

themes.title: Anthropic turns profit again, picks Nasdaq; OpenAI skips 2026
themes.summary: Anthropic told shareholders it expects a second consecutive quarter of adjusted operating profit and has chosen Nasdaq for what could be a record IPO, partly to ease cash-burn concerns. By contrast, Sam Altman ruled out an OpenAI IPO in 2026 as fears over AI risk dominate headlines. A liquid public pricing benchmark for frontier AI is taking shape.
themes.angle: The first frontier-lab profit-and-listing story gives institutions a benchmark for pricing the whole sector.

themes.title: Washington scrambles: Congress won't lead, Democrats move
themes.summary: House Speaker Johnson said Congress will not take the lead on AI safety and urged calm, hours before Democrats scheduled a Tuesday caucus on AI action and Barack Obama pushed oversight up the party's agenda. Meanwhile the biggest labs quietly discussed a voluntary safety-standards body, and AI-focused political action committees multiplied ahead of the midterms.
themes.angle: With the executive branch downplaying risk and Congress declining the lead, AI oversight is becoming a US election issue.

themes.title: GCC runs its own race: energy-AI pacts, jobs, regulation
themes.summary: The UAE and Germany sealed energy and AI partnerships that could enable EUR5bn of investment, while a Khaleej Times report argues AI is reshaping rather than eliminating GCC jobs. Arab News asks whether governments can regulate AI without slowing innovation, and LG opened its first Middle East B2B AI home space in Saudi Arabia, signalling consumer-adjacent AI demand.
themes.angle: Gulf governments are positioning as regulators-without-a-brake - a deliberate contrast to Washington's slowdown fight.

themes.title: Agents move from demo to production: Perplexity on GPT-6 Astra
themes.summary: OpenAI's blog details Perplexity running communications, software changes and production monitoring end-to-end on GPT-6 Astra with far less human check-in - a credible enterprise reference point for long-running agents. It matches Anthropic's push toward long-horizon agentic workloads and raises questions about how much automation boards should accept without new guardrails.
themes.angle: A public production deployment, not a benchmark, is the strongest evidence yet that long-running agents are ready for enterprise workflows.

themes.title: AI infrastructure meets the ballot box
themes.summary: Texas is slowing data-centre approvals as public backlash threatens midterm hopes, Amazon and Microsoft are backing communities against utilities over power, and investors publicly treat the AI slowdown call as a temporary step. AI's physical footprint is becoming a local political issue even as its financial backers stay committed.
themes.angle: Power, permits and politics - the least-reported constraint on AI buildout is now a voter issue in the US.
